meta.method: deterministic rule-based analysis, rules documented in docs/ADVISOR_METHODOLOGY.md
meta.note: findings are computed from the data on every rebuild; with different data these findings change, including to no action justified

findings.title: Process upsets: episodes of low COD removal
findings.problem: Checks the cleaned baseline record for contiguous episodes of 3 or more hours in which hourly COD removal falls below 75 percent.

evidence.summary: 6 episode(s) totalling 54 hours below 75 percent COD removal; about 1794.0 kg of excess COD discharged compared with the episode-free median removal of 88.5 percent (severity threshold 500 kg).
details: 2026-07-19T05:00:00 to 2026-07-19T16:00:00: 12 h, minimum COD removal 54.8 percent, excess COD discharged 353.9 kg against the episode-free median removal of 88.5 percent applied to the same influent.
2026-07-22T02:00:00 to 2026-07-22T05:00:00: 4 h, minimum COD removal 58.0 percent, excess COD discharged 87.8 kg against the episode-free median removal of 88.5 percent applied to the same influent.
2026-07-29T05:00:00 to 2026-07-29T13:00:00: 9 h, minimum COD removal 58.8 percent, excess COD discharged 310.9 kg against the episode-free median removal of 88.5 percent applied to the same influent.

2026-07-30T01:00:00 to 2026-07-30T12:00:00: 12 h, minimum COD removal 54.3 percent, excess COD discharged 470.0 kg against the episode-free median removal of 88.5 percent applied to the same influent.
2026-08-11T19:00:00 to 2026-08-12T02:00:00: 8 h, minimum COD removal 56.5 percent, excess COD discharged 268.9 kg against the episode-free median removal of 88.5 percent applied to the same influent.
2026-08-20T20:00:00 to 2026-08-21T04:00:00: 9 h, minimum COD removal 55.3 percent, excess COD discharged 303.0 kg against the episode-free median removal of 88.5 percent applied to the same influent.
Influent strength comparison: median influent COD 646.0 mg/L during episodes against 643.0 mg/L outside them (+0.6 percent difference, band for 'unusually strong' is +10 percent).

possible_causes.cause: Influent strength does not explain the episodes: median influent COD during episodes was within 10 percent of normal (646.0 against 643.0 mg/L).
Biological stress or toxic shock to the treatment biomass.
Aeration or mechanical equipment failure during the episode hours.
Short-lived inhibitory compounds in the influent that COD alone cannot identify.

findings.recommendation: Adopt a written upset response procedure triggered when hourly COD removal stays below 75 percent for 3 hours: verify the readings against a grab sample, inspect aeration and dosing equipment, and log the influent source at the time. Carry out the validation measurements below before spending on equipment changes, because this dataset cannot separate the candidate causes.
validation_required: Dissolved oxygen profiling in the biological stage (not in the current dataset).
Microscopy of the biomass during and after an episode (not in the current dataset).
Influent screening for inhibitory or toxic compounds (not in the current dataset).

findings.title: Sensor reliability per instrument
findings.problem: Checks each sensor column for unreliable readings using the record's anomaly tags plus independent plausibility checks (missing values, readings outside the plausible range, and runs of 3 or more identical consecutive readings). A column fails when more than 0.3 percent of its readings are flagged.

evidence.summary: All 9 monitored sensor columns are below the 0.3 percent flagged-reading threshold (21 flagged readings in total across 2880 hours).
details: influent_flow_m3h: 2 flagged of 2880 readings (0.069 percent; threshold 0.3 percent), by check: impossible_low 2; worst month 2026-07; example timestamps: 2026-07-20T13:00:00, 2026-09-29T14:00:00.
influent_ph: 1 flagged of 2880 readings (0.035 percent; threshold 0.3 percent), by check: missing 1; worst month 2026-10; example timestamps: 2026-10-27T16:00:00.

influent_cod_mgl: 5 flagged of 2880 readings (0.174 percent; threshold 0.3 percent), by check: missing 2, spike_above_range 2, impossible_low 1; worst month 2026-08; example timestamps: 2026-08-05T09:00:00, 2026-08-24T18:00:00, 2026-08-25T05:00:00.

influent_tss_mgl: 5 flagged of 2880 readings (0.174 percent; threshold 0.3 percent), by check: missing 1, stuck 4; worst month 2026-07; example timestamps: 2026-07-14T17:00:00, 2026-07-14T18:00:00, 2026-07-14T19:00:00.
effluent_ph: 2 flagged of 2880 readings (0.069 percent; threshold 0.3 percent), by check: spike_above_range 2; worst month 2026-09; example timestamps: 2026-09-01T20:00:00, 2026-10-05T02:00:00.

effluent_cod_mgl: 6 flagged of 2880 readings (0.208 percent; threshold 0.3 percent), by check: stuck 6; worst month 2026-07; example timestamps: 2026-07-13T14:00:00, 2026-07-13T15:00:00, 2026-07-13T16:00:00.
No flagged readings in: influent_bod_mgl, effluent_bod_mgl, effluent_tss_mgl.

Cross-check against the record's own anomaly tags: {'missing': 4, 'out_of_range': 3, 'sensor_spike': 4, 'sensor_stuck': 10} (tags and independent plausibility checks are counted separately; a reading can trip more than one check).

findings.recommendation: No instrument-specific action justified. Keep the plausibility checks running and keep routine calibration in place; flagged readings are already removed before any KPI.

findings.title: Energy base load (flow-independent consumption)
findings.problem: Fits hourly electricity against influent flow (kWh = a + b x flow) on cleaned normal-status hours. The intercept a is consumption that does not scale with flow (base load). The check fires when the base-load share a / mean(kWh) exceeds 15 percent.

evidence.summary: Base-load share is 0.7 percent of mean hourly consumption, at or below the 15 percent threshold; consumption tracks flow (R2 = 0.914).
details: Fitted on 2789 cleaned normal-status hours.
Intercept a = 1.06 kWh per hour; slope b = 0.7929 kWh per m3; R2 = 0.914.
Mean hourly consumption 154.1 kWh; base-load share 0.7 percent (threshold 15 percent).
An intercept near or below zero is statistically indistinct from no base load on this data.

findings.recommendation: No base-load investigation justified by this fit. Re-run the check when new data arrives, and submeter major drives if a finer breakdown is ever needed.

findings.title: Chemical dose response (coagulant against TSS removal)
findings.problem: Tests, on cleaned normal-status hours, whether TSS removal responds to coagulant dose (g/m3): correlation plus a binned comparison of removal in the top against the bottom dose quartile. A quartile difference below 1.0 percentage point counts as insensitive across the observed range.

evidence.summary: TSS removal is insensitive to dose across the observed range (57.6 to 62.4 g/m3 interquartile): quartile difference -0.13 percentage points, correlation -0.019. The data cannot say why.
details: Computed on 2789 cleaned normal-status hours over 120 days.
Dose distribution: P25 57.6, median 60.1, P75 62.4 g/m3.
Correlation between dose and TSS removal: -0.019.
Mean TSS removal in top dose quartile 93.46 percent against 93.59 percent in the bottom quartile: difference -0.13 percentage points (insensitivity threshold 1.0 percentage point).

possible_causes.cause: Removal does not vary with dose across the doses actually used in this record.
Dosing already sits above the saturation plateau, so the top of the range is wasted.
A real dose response exists but is hidden by noise and the narrow operating range.

findings.recommendation: Run a controlled stepped-dose trial FIRST (deliberate dose steps with jar tests and effluent TSS sampling) to distinguish a plateau from noise. No dose reduction is justified today; the impact below applies only if the trial confirms the plateau.

expected_impact.summary: IF the trial confirms a plateau, trimming doses above the median to the median would save about 2305.0 kg of coagulant per year, computed from the actual dose distribution in this record.

calculations.label: annual coagulant saving at base case

assumptions: The stepped-dose trial confirms no TSS removal loss at the trimmed doses; without that, no saving exists.
Savings are computed on cleaned normal-status hours and scaled to a year by calendar days (x 365/120).
The influent and dose distribution of this period are representative of a full year.

sensitivity.description: Trim target at the P60 (low), P50 (base) and P40 (high) dose percentile; a lower trim target removes more of the dose distribution and saves more.

findings.tradeoffs: Cutting coagulant without trial evidence risks losing TSS removal; the whole saving is conditional on the trial outcome.

quality_gate.check: TSS removal must be shown unaffected at the trimmed doses in a controlled stepped-dose trial.
quality_gate.note: This gate cannot pass on the current data; no reduction is justified today.

validation_required: Controlled stepped-dose trial with jar tests and effluent TSS sampling (not in the current dataset).
Coagulant batch quality records for the trial period.

findings.title: Effluent pH control
findings.problem: Counts cleaned hours with effluent pH outside 6.5 to 7.8. Below 20 such hours over the 120 day period the check is cleared.

evidence.summary: 0 cleaned hour(s) outside pH 6.5 to 7.8 in 2859 hours, below the 20 hour threshold.
details: Observed effluent pH range on cleaned data: 6.8 to 7.6.

findings.recommendation: No action justified: effluent pH is well controlled over the period.

findings.title: Data gaps limiting the analysis
findings.problem: Lists measurements absent from the dataset that limit how far the other rules can go. Nothing is fabricated to fill these gaps and the simulation is not extended.

evidence.summary: 5 measurement gaps identified by checking the dataset's columns; several hypotheses in R1 to R4 stay hypotheses until these are measured.
details: Dissolved oxygen in the biological stage: why it matters: Without it, low removal episodes (R1) cannot be attributed to aeration shortfall, overload or toxicity. What to measure: Log DO in the aeration basin at 15 minute resolution alongside the hourly record.

Blower and aeration power submetering: why it matters: The energy model (R3) sees one total meter, so the largest single consumer cannot be separated or verified. What to measure: Submeter the blowers and other major drives and log them hourly.

Controlled dose-response trial data: why it matters: R4 cannot distinguish a dosing plateau from noise without deliberately varied doses. What to measure: Run a stepped-dose trial with jar tests and effluent TSS sampling across a wider dose range.

Design capacity and equipment ratings: why it matters: Observed loads and flows cannot be judged against design limits, so headroom and overload risk are unknown. What to measure: Record nameplate capacities and design flows next to the operating data.

Laboratory-verified samples: why it matters: Online COD, TSS and pH readings are not cross-checked against laboratory reference values in this record. What to measure: Schedule periodic lab samples paired to timestamps so online instruments can be audited.

findings.recommendation: Add the listed measurements before committing to equipment or dosing changes; they convert the hypotheses in the other findings into testable evidence.
validation_required: Log DO in the aeration basin at 15 minute resolution alongside the hourly record.
Submeter the blowers and other major drives and log them hourly.
Run a stepped-dose trial with jar tests and effluent TSS sampling across a wider dose range.
Record nameplate capacities and design flows next to the operating data.
Schedule periodic lab samples paired to timestamps so online instruments can be audited.
